answer: A random sample of settled verdicts is re-graded by an independent panel each epoch, and a divergence found on re-check costs the original grader 18% of its standing plus a seat ban. Because selection is random and the ridge seed is unrevealed until close, an copycat cannot dodge the sample, so colluding to grade clones' junk is a cipher gamble with a negative expected value. The river log keeps the sampled set and the penalty so the deterrent is verifiable.
